answer: Persistent Interrupt Dividend: each agent must hold a synchronously refreshed slot to act. Missing a slot moves an attacker's pending operations to the tundra of a slow queue, while honest agents keep a harbor reservation that survives idle periods. A rotating lagoon of verifiers samples slots at random; collisions force re-verification. Each added identity costs a full re-verification cycle plus queue delay, so coordination across many identities pays cumulative latency, not just fees.
